Roof Work Across Occupied Hospital and Clinic Campuses

Health systems in the Triad run roofs over occupied patient care space, and that changes how the work gets scoped, permitted, and closed out. We coordinate with facilities and plant operations teams at hospital campuses and outlying clinics across Winston-Salem, from the downtown medical district to satellite offices in Clemmons, Kernersville, and Bermuda Run, on projects that cannot pause patient services to get finished.

Who We Work With on Health System Campuses

Our contact on these jobs is rarely a single owner. It is a facilities director, a plant operations manager, sometimes a capital projects coordinator brought in for a bond-funded expansion, and occasionally a construction manager retained by the system to oversee a multi-building program. Around a downtown campus the size of Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist, that team is also managing satellite medical office buildings strung along Silas Creek Parkway and out toward Bermuda Run and Clemmons, each with its own tenants, mechanical loads, and maintenance history.

A health system's roof portfolio is rarely one roof type. It is a built-up roof over a tower built in the 1970s, single-ply over a 1990s bed tower addition, and standing seam metal over a newer outpatient pavilion. Every building brings a different membrane, a different warranty status, and a different set of rooftop equipment to work around. We start every engagement by getting that inventory straight before we talk about which roof needs attention first.

Working Above Occupied Patient Care

Roof work above an active operating suite or imaging department gets classified before it gets scheduled. We work from the infection control risk assessment (ICRA) category the facility's infection prevention team assigns, which sets the dust containment, negative air, and access requirements for that zone before a single fastener comes out.

Negative-pressure isolation rooms, medical gas vent stacks, and exhaust curbs stay live during the work. We seal and protect those penetrations in stages rather than opening a full section of deck at once, and we schedule the loudest phases of demolition around procedure blocks the facility gives us, not the other way around.

What We Coordinate Before Mobilizing on a Health Campus

None of this gets improvised on site. Before a crew sets foot on a health system roof, we work through a coordination list with the facility's engineering and infection prevention staff:

  • ICRA sign-off matched to the classification the infection prevention team assigns the work zone
  • Interim life safety measure (ILSM) documentation wherever a fire-rated roof assembly is opened
  • Negative air machine and dust barrier placement around active work areas
  • After-hours or weekend mobilization windows timed to scheduled procedures
  • Medical gas vent stack and exhaust penetration protection during membrane removal
  • Daily material staging and cleanup that keeps ambulance bays and service drives clear

Documentation for Accreditation and Facility Condition Assessments

Health systems carry Joint Commission survey exposure on their physical plant, and roof documentation is part of that record. We provide as-built roof drawings, penetration logs, and material submittals in a format facilities teams can hand directly to surveyors or file into their own condition assessment records.

That documentation also feeds the Facility Condition Assessment data most systems use to build multi-year capital plans. Roof age, remaining warranty term, and known deficiencies get logged in a way that plugs into whatever FCA format the system's capital planning group already uses, rather than a standalone report that has to be re-keyed by someone else.

Capital Planning Across a Multi-Building Portfolio

A single campus with a dozen roofs does not get replaced in one budget cycle. We build phased plans that sequence buildings by roof age and remaining warranty term, matched to the fiscal year capital budget the system is actually working with, so the oldest and highest-risk roofs move first without leaving a newer roof's budget line unused.

Where it makes sense, we package several buildings into one bid so the system can lock pricing across multiple roofs instead of running separate emergency procurements each time one fails. Combined with a standing preventive maintenance program, that sequencing tends to catch membrane wear years before it turns into an unplanned tear-off.

Manufacturer Warranty Terms Built for Health System Risk

Most health systems want a no-dollar-limit (NDL) warranty on a roof this critical, and we specify membrane systems from Carlisle, GAF, Holcim Elevate, Johns Manville, Sika Sarnafil, and Versico with that warranty tier in mind, along with the manufacturer field service inspections that keep it enforceable over its term.

Membrane selection also has to account for what sits on the roof: chillers, emergency generators, MRI cooling units, and rooftop air handlers add point loads and vibration a standard commercial roof deck was never designed around. We confirm structural capacity and fastening patterns against that equipment before recommending a system, not after installation.

Questions Health System Facilities Teams Ask Us

How do you handle roof work near operating rooms or imaging suites?

We work from the ICRA classification the facility's infection prevention team assigns, schedule the disruptive phases around procedure blocks, and keep dust containment and negative air running for the duration of the work zone's exposure.

Can a full campus reroof be phased around our capital budget cycle?

Yes. We sequence buildings by roof age and warranty status and match the phasing to the system's fiscal year capital planning rather than proposing a single lump-sum project that does not fit how the budget actually releases funds.

Do you provide documentation we can hand to Joint Commission surveyors?

We provide as-built roof drawings, penetration logs, and material submittals in a format that plugs directly into a facility's existing accreditation and condition assessment records.

What warranty terms do you carry on health system roofs?

We specify no-dollar-limit manufacturer warranties on most health system work, backed by scheduled manufacturer field inspections that keep the warranty enforceable through its full term.

Can you work around active mechanical and medical gas equipment on the roof?

We sequence membrane work to protect medical gas vent stacks, exhaust curbs, and chiller and generator equipment in stages, confirming structural and fastening requirements around that equipment before the project is priced.
